# Bool output for integral SumDims: source-only candidate

This isolated candidate extends command 115 only for Bool and I64 input with an explicit Bool destination. It is based on the frozen 699-function runtime afd54444849ed10f7b4af53231c9db6542854b70f33e3927f8b05dfbb23ed1e3. The original 699 source, image, reference24 and five dtype controls remain historical originals.

## Concrete implementation

The candidate adds the real HIA function sb_sum_bool. It reuses the bound sd_axis_mask, si_plan, tget and taddr bodies. It creates a fresh owning Bool Tensor with typed_descriptor(..., 0, 1, 1), initializes every output byte to zero, converts each logical input value to canonical zero/one before accumulation, and uses bit.or for Bool addition. This is the Bool operation selected by the fixed CPU SumKernel; it cannot turn integer cancellation or overflow into false. Logical iteration follows actual input strides and offsets, including holes, overlap and zero stride.

The original si_sum_integral body is untouched. si_dispatch_sum gets one explicit dtype1 branch inside its existing Bool/I64-input branch. to_command admits dtype1 while preserving all other packet checks and their order. Four format functions change only HTSINT01/HTOSIN01 to HTSINT02/HTOSIN02. The ABI remains 672 bytes. The prospective body inventory is 700 functions: 693 old bodies unchanged, six old bodies changed, one body added. No actual emission or compiler count is claimed.

The addition is mechanically derived from the complete, actual si_sum_integral HIA body with seven exact edits. body-derivation.json records those edits and the six existing-body edits. body-patch.json contains every before/after body, the complete 699-body inventory and original order, and the future whole-runtime inverse specification. The original integer function remains an independent body.

## Source evidence

The official source review pins sixteen complete files from PyTorch commit 31a77fc9c0a7c6fff15a1ff58c743f53b1a9d457. Explicit Bool chooses a Bool reduction input; I64 is converted before reduction. Bool addition stores back to Bool and has false identity. None/[] and signed-axis handling follow the existing axis helpers. Bool cannot require gradients.

The helper basis contains eleven complete HIA bodies read from immutable Git blob 8c61bb4667af857b0dafe7077c5fe88d291dd6fd (c436 parent) and individually SHA-matched to the actual699 body ledger. It covers real one-byte allocation, new Storage/Version, strided reads, byte stores, and public Tensor publication.

## Future source application

The following command is a source-construction interface, not an executed request:

    python -I -S -B apply_source.py --parent-runtime ORIGINAL_699/runtime.hepta --package THIS_PACKAGE --output NEW_SOURCE_DIRECTORY

The input must be the exact 2312858-byte, mode0600 parent. The package is intended to be materialized with mode0644 for every listed payload. apply_source.py verifies the complete payload set, full parent bytes and all 699 body hashes before constructing a new runtime. It requires a fresh output directory, preserves all unmodified bodies, and proves forward and inverse whole-byte equality in the future output report. It does not parse a Python AST, run an emitter, generate module units, invoke a compiler, execute a Tensor image, or calculate an expected Tensor result. Its Python source has not been imported, AST-checked or executed in this task.

## Qualification boundary

This package is CACHE_ONLY / SOURCE_ONLY_NOT_APPLIED. The local string-level body forward/inverse checks were completed; the whole runtime application awaits the actual parent bytes in a future authorized invocation. New HIA syntax/type verification, unit generation, cold compilation, reference observation, native replay and owner/resource gates have not run.

A new fixed-PyTorch reference is required for Bool raw values, shape/stride, one-byte Storage, Version, no-AD and measured lifetimes. The old I64 output observer cannot be generalized by accepting any width. A new observer must explicitly check Bool output and preserve all old predicates. future-qualification-contract.json proposes a new seven-control denominator; it does not change the old five-control source or results. No old PASS is transferred.

# Proposed Bool destination extension of command 115

State format: HTSINT02. Backing format: HTOSIN02. Descriptor: 672 bytes. No new command number or autograd opcode is allocated.

The existing eight-u64 command layout is retained:
- word 0: 115
- word 1: public Tensor token, decoded by the original public_node path
- word 2: dimension count; UINT64_MAX means None, zero means []
- word 3: dimension payload offset, zero for None/[]
- word 4: keepdim, zero or one
- word 5: destination dtype; the new value is 1 for Bool
- words 6 and 7: reserved zero

Nonempty dimension lists retain the original payload-bound checks and signed-u64 axis representation. None and [] are separate input forms but both reduce all dimensions in this operation. The existing rank0..4, nonnegative-stride and 262144-logical-element finite contract remains. The source must be Bool or I64 and must not require gradients. Other destination/source combinations retain their original dispatch except for these two new explicit Bool cases.

The Bool branch computes the original dimension mask before si_plan clears the shared scratch range. It allocates a new owning output with dtype1 and requires=0. It does not retain the source, record op47, create a Saved variable, alias the input Storage, or create a gradient accumulator. The output raw element is canonical 0/1 and uses one byte. I64 is converted by testing the complete u64 value for zero before Bool addition; there is no low-byte truncation and no integer sum before conversion. Every logical source element is visited, so source bounds checks are retained even after an output becomes true.

Output rank, size, contiguous strides and output element count come from the original si_plan and typed_descriptor bodies. Empty reductions retain the false identity, including a nonempty output arising from a zero reduced extent. An empty output has zero data bytes but still follows the genuine owning Tensor/Storage/Version constructor. Version behavior is a pending new actual-reference obligation, not a guessed final constant.

All original error and rollback contracts remain required for invalid capabilities, dimensions, packet payload and allocation failure. The raw HIA patch preserves every existing packet check; newly admitted dtype1 packets must receive their own actual entry controls. No native execution or error outcome is claimed by this source package.

"""Apply the frozen Bool-output HIA patch; source construction only, no Tensor evaluation."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import stat
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

PATCH_SHA256 = "3fd037205b00fd6341408b2b5a12799d87893f2fae892038de9cfcb8c0ed045b"
PARENT_SHA256 = "afd54444849ed10f7b4af53231c9db6542854b70f33e3927f8b05dfbb23ed1e3"
FUNCTION = re.compile(
    rb"^(fn ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\([^\n]* entry\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\)\n.*?^end\n)",
    re.M | re.S,
)
CALL = re.compile(rb'\{"function":"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)"\}')
MODIFIED = {
    "state_header", "init_state", "so_state_init", "so_state_header",
    "to_command", "si_dispatch_sum",
}
ADDED = {"sb_sum_bool"}
PRESERVED = {
    "si_plan", "si_sum_integral", "sd_axis_mask", "sd_sum_tensor",
    "sd_execute_plan", "sd_backward", "typed_descriptor",
    "scalar_previous_typed_descriptor", "dtype_width", "tget", "taddr",
    "typed_load", "typed_store", "alloc", "so_slot_new",
    "gradient_accumulate", "incoming_describe", "partial_apply_node",
    "publish_tensor", "shape_command_finish", "entry",
}

def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()

def read_bound(path, expected_sha=None, expected_bytes=None, expected_mode=None):
    path = Path(path)
    assert path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink(), str(path)
    before = path.stat()
    assert stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode)
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    after = path.stat()
    identity = lambda s: (
        s.st_dev, s.st_ino, s.st_size, s.st_mtime_ns, s.st_ctime_ns,
        stat.S_IMODE(s.st_mode),
    )
    assert identity(before) == identity(after), str(path)
    actual = {
        "path": str(path.resolve()), "bytes": len(raw), "sha256": sha(raw),
        "mode": stat.S_IMODE(after.st_mode),
    }
    if expected_sha is not None:
        assert actual["sha256"] == expected_sha, (str(path), actual["sha256"])
    if expected_bytes is not None:
        assert len(raw) == expected_bytes, (str(path), len(raw))
    if expected_mode is not None:
        assert actual["mode"] == expected_mode, (str(path), actual["mode"])
    return raw, actual

def parse_source(raw):
    matches = list(FUNCTION.finditer(raw))
    assert matches
    names = [m[2].decode("ascii") for m in matches]
    assert len(names) == len(set(names))
    functions = {m[2].decode("ascii"): m[1] for m in matches}
    header = raw[:matches[0].start()]
    assert header + b"".join(functions.values()) == raw
    return header, functions

def write_new(path, raw):
    assert isinstance(raw, bytes)
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
            stream.write(raw)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
    except BaseException:
        raise
    metadata = {
        "bytes": len(raw), "sha256": sha(raw),
        "mode": stat.S_IMODE(Path(path).stat().st_mode),
    }
    assert metadata["mode"] == 0o600 and Path(path).read_bytes() == raw
    return metadata

def json_bytes(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n").encode("ascii")

def apply_exact(parent_raw, patch):
    assert patch["schema"] == "heptatorch.sum-bool.exact-source-body-patch.v1"
    assert patch["status"] == "SOURCE_ONLY_NOT_APPLIED"
    assert patch["parent"]["source_sha256"] == PARENT_SHA256
    assert len(parent_raw) == patch["parent"]["bytes"] == 2312858
    assert sha(parent_raw) == PARENT_SHA256
    parent_header, parent = parse_source(parent_raw)
    assert parent_header == patch["parent_header"].encode("ascii")
    assert len(parent) == patch["parent"]["functions"] == 699
    assert list(parent) == patch["parent_function_order"]
    assert set(parent) == set(patch["parent_body_sha256"])
    assert {name: sha(body) for name, body in parent.items()} == patch["parent_body_sha256"]
    changes = patch["changed_functions"]
    additions = patch["added_functions"]
    assert len(changes) == 6 and {x["name"] for x in changes} == MODIFIED
    assert len(additions) == 1 and {x["name"] for x in additions} == ADDED
    assert ADDED.isdisjoint(parent)
    child = dict(parent)
    for row in changes:
        name = row["name"]
        before = row["before_body"].encode("ascii")
        after = row["after_body"].encode("ascii")
        assert parent[name] == before and sha(before) == row["before_sha256"]
        assert sha(after) == row["after_sha256"] and before != after
        _, parsed = parse_source(after)
        assert list(parsed) == [name] and parsed[name] == after
        child[name] = after
    for row in additions:
        body = row["body"].encode("ascii")
        assert sha(body) == row["sha256"]
        _, parsed = parse_source(body)
        assert list(parsed) == [row["name"]]
        assert parsed[row["name"]] == body
        child[row["name"]] = body
    unchanged = set(parent) - MODIFIED
    assert len(unchanged) == 693
    assert patch["unchanged_functions"] == [
        {"name": name, "sha256": sha(parent[name])}
        for name in parent if name in unchanged
    ]
    assert all(child[name] == parent[name] for name in unchanged)
    assert PRESERVED <= unchanged
    assert list(child) == patch["child_function_order"]
    assert len(child) == patch["prospective"]["functions"] == 700
    assert patch["prospective"]["descriptor_bytes"] == 672
    assert patch["prospective"]["state_format"] == "HTSINT02"
    assert patch["prospective"]["backing_format"] == "HTOSIN02"
    for name in MODIFIED | ADDED:
        dependencies = {m[1].decode("ascii") for m in CALL.finditer(child[name])}
        assert dependencies <= set(child), (name, sorted(dependencies - set(child)))
    child_header = patch["child_header"].encode("ascii")
    assert child_header == b"hia-asm.v1 hepta.hia.program.v8 sum_integral_bool_runtime\n"
    runtime = child_header + b"".join(child.values())
    actual_header, actual = parse_source(runtime)
    assert actual_header == child_header and actual == child
    restored = dict(actual)
    for row in changes:
        assert restored[row["name"]] == row["after_body"].encode("ascii")
        restored[row["name"]] = row["before_body"].encode("ascii")
    for row in additions:
        assert restored[row["name"]] == row["body"].encode("ascii")
        del restored[row["name"]]
    recovered = parent_header + b"".join(restored[name] for name in parent)
    assert recovered == parent_raw and sha(recovered) == PARENT_SHA256
    forwarded = dict(parent)
    for row in changes:
        forwarded[row["name"]] = row["after_body"].encode("ascii")
    for row in additions:
        forwarded[row["name"]] = row["body"].encode("ascii")
    assert child_header + b"".join(forwarded.values()) == runtime
    inverse = {
        "schema": "heptatorch.sum-bool.whole-runtime-inverse.v1",
        "status": "SOURCE_APPLIED_NOT_COMPILED",
        "parent_source_sha256": PARENT_SHA256,
        "child_source_sha256": sha(runtime),
        "parent_header": parent_header.decode("ascii"),
        "child_header": child_header.decode("ascii"),
        "parent_function_order": list(parent), "child_function_order": list(child),
        "changed_functions": changes, "added_functions": additions,
        "unchanged_functions": patch["unchanged_functions"],
        "whole_forward_exact": True, "whole_inverse_exact": True,
        "old_count": 699, "current_count": 700, "unchanged_count": 693,
        "modified_count": 6, "added_count": 1,
        "compiler_executed": False, "native_executed": False, "torch_executed": False,
    }
    return runtime, inverse

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--parent-runtime", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--package", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    assert not args.output.exists(), "Output must be a new directory"
    package = args.package.resolve()
    manifest_raw, manifest_info = read_bound(package / "source-manifest.json")
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_raw)
    assert manifest["schema"] == "heptatorch.sum-bool.source-package.v1"
    assert manifest["status"] == "SOURCE_ONLY_NOT_APPLIED"
    assert manifest["parent_source_sha256"] == PARENT_SHA256
    declared = manifest["files"]
    assert manifest["self_exclusions"] == ["source-manifest.json"]
    files = list(package.rglob("*"))
    assert not any(p.is_symlink() for p in files)
    actual_names = {str(p.relative_to(package)) for p in files if p.is_file()}
    assert actual_names == set(declared) | {"source-manifest.json"}
    input_bindings = {manifest_info["path"]: manifest_info}
    payloads = {}
    for name, item in declared.items():
        relative = Path(name)
        assert not relative.is_absolute() and ".." not in relative.parts
        raw, metadata = read_bound(package / relative, item["sha256"], item["bytes"], item["mode"])
        payloads[name] = raw
        input_bindings[metadata["path"]] = metadata
    assert manifest["payload_count"] == len(payloads)
    assert manifest["payload_bytes"] == sum(map(len, payloads.values()))
    assert (package / "apply_source.py").resolve() == Path(__file__).resolve()
    assert sha(payloads["body-patch.json"]) == PATCH_SHA256
    patch = json.loads(payloads["body-patch.json"])
    parent_raw, parent_info = read_bound(
        args.parent_runtime, PARENT_SHA256, 2312858, 0o600,
    )
    input_bindings[parent_info["path"]] = parent_info
    runtime, inverse = apply_exact(parent_raw, patch)
    for path, item in input_bindings.items():
        read_bound(path, item["sha256"], item["bytes"], item["mode"])
    args.output.mkdir(parents=False, exist_ok=False)
    emitted = {}
    primary_error = None
    try:
        emitted["runtime.hepta"] = write_new(args.output / "runtime.hepta", runtime)
        emitted["integral01-to-bool01-body-inverse.json"] = write_new(
            args.output / "integral01-to-bool01-body-inverse.json", json_bytes(inverse),
        )
        emitted["inputs-before.json"] = write_new(
            args.output / "inputs-before.json", json_bytes(input_bindings),
        )
        after = {}
        for path, item in input_bindings.items():
            _, after[path] = read_bound(path, item["sha256"], item["bytes"], item["mode"])
        assert after == input_bindings
        emitted["inputs-after.json"] = write_new(
            args.output / "inputs-after.json", json_bytes(after),
        )
    except BaseException:
        primary_error = traceback.format_exc()
    report = {
        "schema": "heptatorch.sum-bool.source-application.v1",
        "status": "FAIL" if primary_error else "PASS_SOURCE_APPLICATION_ONLY",
        "parent_source_sha256": PARENT_SHA256,
        "package_manifest": manifest_info, "patch_sha256": PATCH_SHA256,
        "source_sha256": sha(runtime), "functions": 700, "descriptor_bytes": 672,
        "state_format": "HTSINT02", "backing_format": "HTOSIN02",
        "changed_functions": sorted(MODIFIED), "added_functions": sorted(ADDED),
        "unchanged_parent_count": 693,
        "whole_forward_exact": True, "whole_inverse_exact": True,
        "input_bindings": input_bindings,
        "all_inputs_unchanged": primary_error is None,
        "files": emitted, "primary_error": primary_error,
        "unit_generation_executed": False, "ast_executed": False,
        "compiler_executed": False, "native_executed": False, "torch_executed": False,
        "numeric_expectations_computed_by_host": False,
        "runtime_qualified": False, "schema_closure": False, "full_project_status": "HOLD",
    }
    write_new(args.output / "report.json", json_bytes(report))
    return 1 if primary_error else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
